options.name: Progression Balancing
options.doc:
A system that can move progression earlier, to try and prevent the player from getting stuck and bored early.

A lower setting means more getting stuck. A higher setting means less getting stuck.
options.doc_html:
A system that can move progression earlier, to try and prevent the player from getting stuck and bored early.

A lower setting means more getting stuck. A higher setting means less getting stuck.

options.name: Accessibility
options.doc:
Set rules for reachability of your items/locations.

**Full:** ensure everything can be reached and acquired.

**Minimal:** ensure what is needed to reach your goal can be acquired.
options.doc_html:
Set rules for reachability of your items/locations.

Full: ensure everything can be reached and acquired.

Minimal: ensure what is needed to reach your goal can be acquired.

options.name: Expanded Item Pool
options.doc:
Determines if places other than chests and special weapons will be locations.
This includes boss fights as well as powering the tesla orb and completing the console login.
In Expanded Pool, system power is instead restored when receiving the System Power item.
Similarly, the final area door will open once the four Key items, one for each main area, have been found.

options.name: Trap Chance
options.doc: Likelihood of a filler item becoming a trap.

options.name: Death Link
options.doc: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.
options.doc_html: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.

options.name: Instant Saving
options.doc:
When enabled, save points activate with no delay when touched.
This makes saving much faster, at the cost of being unable to pick and choose when to save in order to save warp.

options.name: Sprint Availability
options.doc:
Determines under which conditions the debug sprint is made accessible to the player.
To sprint, hold down Ctrl if playing on keyboard, or Left Bumper if on gamepad (remappable).
With Jacket: you will not be able to sprint until after the Jacket item has been found.

options.name: Cliff Weapon Upgrade
options.doc:
Determines which weapon Cliff uses against you, base or upgraded.
This does not change the available strategies all that much.
Vanilla: Cliff adds fire to his grenades if Ace has been defeated.
If playing with the expanded pool, the Arctic Key will trigger the change instead.

options.name: Ace Weapon Upgrade
options.doc:
Determines which weapon Ace uses against you, base or upgraded.
Ace with his base weapon is very hard to dodge, the upgraded weapon offers a more balanced experience.
Vanilla: Ace uses ice attacks if Cliff has been defeated.
If playing with the expanded pool, the Volcanic Key will trigger the change instead.

options.name: IFrame Duration %
options.doc:
Percentage multiplier for Portia's invincibility frames.
0% means you will have no invincibility frames.
100% means invincibility frames will be the same as vanilla.

options.name: Screen Shake Intensity %
options.doc:
Percentage multiplier for screen shake effects.
0% means the screen will not shake at all.
100% means the screen shake will be the same as in vanilla.

options.name: Music Shuffle
options.doc:
Enables music shuffling.
The title screen song is not shuffled, as it plays before the client connects.

options.name: Local Items
options.doc: Forces these items to be in their native world.
options.doc_html: Forces these items to be in their native world.

options.name: Non-local Items
options.doc: Forces these items to be outside their native world.
options.doc_html: Forces these items to be outside their native world.

options.name: Start Inventory
options.doc: Start with the specified amount of these items. Example: {Bomb: 1, Arrow: 3}
options.doc_html: Start with the specified amount of these items. Example: {Bomb: 1, Arrow: 3}

options.name: Start Inventory from Pool
options.doc:
Start with the specified amount of these items and don't place them in the world. Example: {Bomb: 1, Arrow: 3}

The game decides what the replacement items will be.
options.doc_html:
Start with the specified amount of these items and don't place them in the world. Example: {Bomb: 1, Arrow: 3}

The game decides what the replacement items will be.

options.name: Start Hints
options.doc: Start with these item's locations prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.
options.doc_html: Start with these item's locations prefilled into the !hint command.

options.name: Start Location Hints
options.doc: Start with these locations and their item prefilled into the ``!hint`` command.
options.doc_html: Start with these locations and their item prefilled into the !hint command.

options.name: Excluded Locations
options.doc: Prevent these locations from having an important item.
options.doc_html: Prevent these locations from having an important item.

options.name: Priority Locations
options.doc: Prevent these locations from having an unimportant item.
options.doc_html: Prevent these locations from having an unimportant item.

options.doc: Share part of your item pool with other players.
